context: Rejections re-adjudicated after the owner removed 3 invariants and 2 reasoning patterns on 2026-08-16. reasonStatus records whether the ORIGINAL reason is VOIDED/WEAKENED/SURVIVES.

items.oldReason: "Fleet / multi-key patterns … the ratified 'credentials stay user-operated' invariant rules out key rotation and account pooling; the alternative — one provider entry per credential — already exists" (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:375-381). Bundled with C4's "a random draw cannot answer 'why this backend' reproducibly; the un-blended /candidates invariant forbids a second composite score" (:364-371).
items.rationale: Two of the three legs are struck. The credential leg is void. The "no second composite score" leg was ALREADY self-contradicted: llm-relay has had a weighted composite since deploymentFitness (0.75*capability + 0.2*operational + 0.05*metadata, src/benchmarks.ts:220) — the un-blended rule only ever governed the /candidates TABLE, not pool ordering. What survives is independent and still in force: freellmapi's key ordering is a stochastic draw (sampleBeta per request, server/src/services/router.ts:1073), and reproducibility is the project's Transparency goal (docs/project-goals.md:16-18), which the owner did not strike. A per-request random draw makes "why did this key serve?" unanswerable after the fact — the same objection that killed exact-response caching's audit story, and unrelated to credentials. The DETERMINISTIC residue of this item (order keys you hold by observed evidence) is real and is folded into credential pooling below; only the sampler is rejected.

items.item: Credential pooling — multiple keys per provider (#619/#640)
items.oldReason: Same paragraph: the invariant "rules out key rotation and account pooling"; "the alternative — one provider entry per credential — already exists and keeps health/facts/provenance per credential" (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:375-381).
items.rationale: The invariant leg is struck outright. Note also that the ToS text it rested on never covered this case: the operative sentence is about offering "Claude.ai login or … Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users" (docs/codex-review-2026-08-05.md:32-34) — third-party provider keys the operator holds himself are not that. The "alternative already exists" leg is technically true but thin: ProviderConfig carries exactly one authEnv (src/config.ts:67), so two keys means two provider entries, which duplicates catalog fetches and — more importantly — splits health, target-facts and quota accounting across two identities. Adapt rather than adopt: add an ordered `authEnvs?: string[]` to ProviderConfig, resolved through the existing closed alias list in authEnv.ts (never a key-shaped env scan), with DETERMINISTIC selection — first credential not credential-faulted and not over a ledger gate — and make the credential a component of the breaker/fact key so `credential-invalid` and `allowance-exhausted` stop being provider-wide when a provider has several. Prior art: freellmapi rotates a key pool per platform at server/src/services/router.ts:1140-1175 (round-robin at :1153, per-key cooldown/cap gates at :1161-1173). Sequence this AFTER the ledger: with one key per provider (this install's current shape) the ledger alone delivers the accounting value and this delivers none.

items.oldReason: Bundled into the same "fleet / multi-key" credential-invariant paragraph (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:375-381) and restated in status-vs-freellmapi-2026-08-16.md:190-192 alongside encrypted key storage.
items.rationale: The credential-custody leg is void, and freellmapi's implementation is only incidentally about credentials (it encrypts the proxy URL because it may carry user:pass, lib/key-proxy.ts:1-11). What survives is an independent footprint reason that the owner did not strike (rejection-ledger group B): llm-relay routes every backend call through global fetch, which has no proxy support — per-key egress needs an explicit undici ProxyAgent plus a SOCKS agent, taking the project from two pure-JS runtime deps to four, and it would have to be threaded through both fetchBackend and fetchOpenAiFront. Against that, no egress-control need is on record here. Honest classification: this belongs in the ledger's group E (conditional skip), not group C — it reopens the moment the owner needs geo-routing or a corporate egress path, and the reason to name then is dependency cost, not credentials.

items.item: RPM/RPD/TPM/TPD sliding-window ledger (per-key accounting that gates before dispatch)
items.oldReason: Three bundled reasons: (i) the credentials-stay-user-operated invariant; (ii) "a second, *predictive* quota policy beside the breaker's reactive one" / one place per policy; (iii) "a ledger presupposes limits free providers don't publish" (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:375-381; docs/status-vs-freellmapi-2026-08-16.md:183-185).
items.rationale: Legs (i) and (ii) are both struck — and the ledger-as-custody framing was always a category error: metering keys you already hold is accounting, not custody. Leg (iii) is the only fact-about-the-world and it is FALSE AS STATED: llm-relay already extracts provider-stated rate-limit headers on live traffic (extractQuotaPercent's seven header variants, src/ping/ping.ts:26-52, wired at src/server.ts:1537), and freellmapi additionally LEARNS ceilings from refusal bodies (parseProviderLimit/learnLimitFromError, services/ratelimit.ts:1125-1157) — structurally identical to llm-relay's own context-limits.ts, which already records only explicitly STATED maxima. Where nothing is published, "unknown ⇒ no gate" is exactly the doctrine llm-relay already applies to the context guardrail; that is a degradation, not a blocker. Decisive: llm-relay is already half-built for this and the half is dead. ModelTelemetry declares totalCompletionTokens (src/ping/runtime-telemetry.ts:22) and backend.ts sets stream_options.include_usage explicitly so that "anything metering off the stream" doesn't undercount (src/backend.ts:492-495) — yet the sole production call site passes no tokens at all: recordModelCall(target.provider, target.model, { ok, latencyMs }) (src/server.ts:1262). Token accounting is a declared field that production never populates. SHAPE: new src/usage-ledger.ts — versioned JSON at ~/.llm-relay/usage-ledger.json flushed through the existing WriteBehindTimer (src/write-behind.ts), no DB; sliding minute/day windows plus lifetime totals keyed (provider, credential, model) with provider-scope rollups; written at the two existing choke points (recordCall, src/server.ts:1259, extended with usage from the parsed message at src/server.ts:2681 and the SSE message_delta; observeAttemptHeaders, src/server.ts:1526, extended to keep raw limit/remaining/reset instead of collapsing to a percent). Every field carries a basis — `stated` (provider header/body) | `learned` (refusal-derived, mirroring context-limits.ts) | `estimated` (estimateRequestTokens, src/metadata.ts:151) — which is the recalibrated guess rule applied correctly: counts are measurements, input estimates are labelled estimates, absent limits stay null. Surface it as `llm-relay usage` + a GET /usage admin route and counters on /telemetry, which today is health-shaped with zero request/token counters (src/telemetry.ts:122-134). ⚠ The pre-dispatch GATE half must DEMOTE, not exclude — "health demotes, never drops" is still in force; the only exclusion-grade signal is a provider-STATED remaining=0 with a reset, which is already the existing cooldown class. Prior art for the gate: freellmapi services/ratelimit.ts:292-330 (canMakeRequest/canUseTokens) called from router.ts:1171-1172. Split delivery: recording (small) → windows + surface (medium) → demotion gate (medium).

items.oldReason: "Account-cap tables would also hardcode provider knowledge in `src/`" plus the credential invariant (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:375-381); restated as C6 in the ledger (:96-98).
items.rationale: Both legs are struck — provider-agnosticism explicitly, credentials explicitly. And this is the item with the strongest MEASURED case already in this repo: CLAUDE.md's "pool depth is not quota independence" gotcha and docs/pool-eligibility.md record pool/xhigh's 15 members resolving to four quota domains, so failover spent 13 round-trips to discover 4 facts. An account cap is the PROACTIVE twin of the reactive `allowance-exhausted` fact llm-relay already learns at provider (= credential) scope in target-facts.ts. Adapt rather than adopt because freellmapi's version is a bare literal table (openrouter: 1000, modelscope: 1800, nvidia: 40 — services/ratelimit.ts:348-372) with no provenance; a policy number attributed to a provider that nobody verified is the one thing the recalibrated guess rule still forbids. SHAPE: `ProviderConfig.accountCaps?: { rpm?, rpd?, tpd? }` beside timeoutMs (src/config.ts:59-98), enforced by the usage ledger at provider/credential scope, basis `operator-declared`. Seeded defaults in presets.ts are now legitimate (the src/-agnosticism rule is struck, and presets.ts already carries per-provider knowledge at src/presets.ts:12) provided they are labelled `preset-default` and overridable — the same bootstrap-not-mechanism pattern as SEED_INTERPRETATIONS (src/refusal-interpretation.ts:417). Small once the ledger exists; near-worthless without it.

items.item: Quota-pool-key platform tables (which models share one quota bucket)
items.oldReason: Credential invariant plus C6 "no hardcoded provider knowledge in src/" (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:380-381; ledger :96-98).
items.rationale: Both stated legs struck. The residue is a genuine design preference, not a blocker: freellmapi's inferPoolForPlatform is ~35 hardcoded platform strings (services/provider-quota.ts:112-149) and it INFERS — which llm-relay's lookup-never-inference doctrine treats as a distinct class. But llm-relay already owns the right primitive: FactScope's `group` kind carries an explicit member list, hashed into its storage key (src/target-facts.ts:83-90,186), and CLAUDE.md already states groups take no prefix inference. A quota pool IS a group. SHAPE: declare pools in config (or reuse the group scope) — e.g. `ProviderConfig.quotaPools?: Record<string, string[]>` — so a provider's members that share one bucket are named, not guessed, and the ledger meters at pool scope. The one mechanical case worth seeding is openrouter's `:free` vs account split (provider-quota.ts:114), which is a suffix rule rather than a name list. Without this the ledger over-counts headroom on shared-pool providers exactly the way the pool-eligibility incident describes.

items.oldReason: Credential invariant, plus an explicit second reason: "the master key would sit in the same directory class as the ciphertext (freellmapi's own dev mode proves the reduction to filesystem ACLs), and the owner's notes already flag the lose-ENCRYPTION_KEY-lose-everything hazard" (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:406-409).
items.rationale: The credential leg is void; the load-bearing leg was never the invariant and it holds — confirmed in freellmapi's OWN source comment, not just llm-relay's summary: "Storing it beside the ciphertext it protects … meant encryption-at-rest protected nothing for a default install: whoever copied the DB also copied the key" (server/src/lib/crypto.ts:22-27). freellmapi's mitigation is a separate 0600 file in the same directory — i.e. it reduces to filesystem ACLs, exactly as recorded. Adding AES-GCM here would buy nothing against a local reader while creating the lose-the-key-lose-12-credentials hazard the owner's own CLAUDE.md already flags for freellmapi. This is the one C1 item whose rejection stands unchanged on its own merits. ADOPTABLE RESIDUE (worth doing, small): llm-relay writes ~/.llm-relay/.env at 0600 only on the onboarding path and only off-Windows (src/onboarding.ts:191-194), while control-token gets FILE_MODE 0600 consistently (src/control-authorization.ts:28,108). On Windows the .env is protected by profile ACL alone and nothing reports that. Add permission enforcement/reporting for .env on the same footing as the control token, and surface its state in `llm-relay keys` — real containment improvement, no crypto.

items.item: client_profiles, part 1 — per-client minted inference keys
items.oldReason: "`client_profiles` is per-client minted keys plus server-enforced system prompts — credential custody, ruled out by the same ratified invariant. *Stating that invariant application out loud, as the goals doc requires.*" (docs/status-vs-freellmapi-2026-08-16.md:194-196).
items.rationale: The custody leg is void, and the mechanism is not the obstacle — llm-relay already mints a 256-bit token with timing-safe comparison and 0600 storage (src/control-authorization.ts). What survives is independent and explicitly still in force: loopback-only bind, and a listener that deliberately does no inference-path auth. Minting per-client INFERENCE keys presupposes multiple mutually-untrusted callers, which a loopback-only single-operator relay structurally does not have; and the client identity llm-relay actually needs it already derives without a credential, from the front-door path (clientForPath / FRONT_DOOR_CLIENTS), which the docs already argue is a stronger signal than any caller-supplied marker. Adding a second authentication surface on the data plane would also require deciding what a request with no profile key means, on a listener whose current answer is "serve it" — a behaviour change with outage risk for zero measured need.

items.oldReason: Same sentence: bundled with minted keys as "credential custody, ruled out by the same ratified invariant" (docs/status-vs-freellmapi-2026-08-16.md:194-196).
items.rationale: This half was mis-bundled: an operator-authored static prompt prefix has nothing to do with credential custody, and the stated reason is entirely void. I considered reviving it under the repair boundary — freellmapi's prependSystemPrompt puts server text ahead of the caller's own system message (server/src/lib/system-prompt.ts:78-82), i.e. the relay authoring conversation content, which is the reason context-handoff injection was rejected. But the boundary as written forbids inserting an LLM's JUDGMENT into the request path, and a fixed operator string is not that. I will not manufacture a replacement reason. What is genuinely undecided is whether the owner wants it: llm-relay already keys per-client behaviour off the front door (routing.offload.<client>), so the routing half exists and only the prompt-mutation half is new — and it would silently change what every model is told, which the Transparency goal (still in force) says must at minimum be announced (an x-llm-relay-* header, as with x-llm-relay-degraded). Ask the owner what it would be for before building; if there is no use, drop it — but drop it for that reason, not the recorded one.

items.item: headroomFactor — the quota-ordering input llm-relay records but never reads
items.oldReason: "ADAPT, not ADOPT: freellmapi's `headroomFactor` is fed by a monthly token ledger already rejected under the credentials-stay-user-operated invariant" (docs/status-vs-freellmapi-2026-08-16.md:122-133); the underlying ledger rejection at :183-185 also cited "a second quota policy beside the breaker".
items.rationale: Both reasons are struck, and the item was never a full rejection — it is already on record as an open ADAPT (medium) on rubric 4. The gap is verified in source: applyHealthOutcome writes state.quotaPercent (src/circuit-breaker.ts:412); the ONLY reader is telemetry.ts:132, for display. targetUsability sees breaker health and credential faults and nothing else (src/server.ts:947-955), and deploymentFitness has no quota term (src/benchmarks.ts:196-227). So the single strongest evidence class this project recognizes — a figure the serving provider stated on real traffic — is the one signal that changes nothing. SHAPE (small, and deliberately not freellmapi's): do NOT multiply deploymentFitness the way freellmapi does (scoring.ts:209-215) — that would let an operational signal move capability order, which orderByUsability's comment at src/server.ts:484-491 exists to prevent. Instead add a fourth band to orderByUsability's existing demotion ladder (src/server.ts:1018-1043): live → low-headroom → credential-fault → cooling, so it demotes and never drops. Absent header ⇒ no opinion ⇒ stays in `live`, matching the neutral-50 doctrine. freellmapi's ramp constants (HEADROOM_RAMP_START 0.2, HEADROOM_FLOOR 0.1, scoring.ts:206-215) are precisely the "tunable constant with a documented default" the recalibrated guess rule now permits — expose the threshold in config, label the basis `provider-stated`, and keep the raw percent visible in /candidates so the demotion is explainable. This is the cheapest large win in the group and it is a natural first slice of the ledger work.

items.item: In-flight concurrency leases / provisional quota gating (Codex ADOPT-HIGH, overruled)
items.oldReason: Three reasons bundled: (a) it is a second, *predictive* quota policy beside the breaker's reactive one — "one place per policy"; (b) "the worst case today is one extra 429 that the walk already absorbs"; (c) llm-relay built and then deleted this exact machinery (the kernel lease budgets removed 2026-08-04, which CLAUDE.md warns against rebuilding). Sources: docs/freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:341-351, docs/rejection-ledger-2026-08-16.md:77-88.
items.rationale: Reason (a) is VOIDED by the directive. Reason (c) is voided by the directive AND is factually a category error: the deleted `AttemptLease` (commit 2b9617f, src/kernel/contracts.ts:167-183) was "a budget-issued, one-shot authority to start one egress attempt" carrying an `ordinal` and `deadline` — a per-request FAILOVER-attempt budget. freellmapi's lease bounds how many requests are simultaneously IN FLIGHT against one credential (server/src/services/ratelimit.ts:60-148). Different mechanism, different problem; "we built and deleted this" was never true of this feature. Reason (b) is the only independent one and it SURVIVES only as an unmeasured estimate — and the source shows the race is structural, not hypothetical. Pool order is materialized once (src/dynamic-pools.ts:265) or served from a 30-second static cache (src/benchmarks.ts:68,315); `orderByUsability` (src/server.ts:1018) re-orders on breaker state, and breaker state mutates only at terminal completion (src/circuit-breaker.ts:309). So N concurrent subagent requests arriving before any completes see byte-identical ordering and all select member #1. The cost is also understated: each of those requests then pays its own full failover walk, and because pool order interleaves providers (src/dynamic-pools.ts:89) each walk burns a DIFFERENT provider's quota — the opposite of the containment the interleave exists for. Against the reinstated accounting goal this is the request-path consumer of a per-key meter, so it should land in the narrow form now and gain provisional token gating only if/when the C1 ledger lands. CONCRETE SHAPE: a new `src/attempt-lease.ts` modelled directly on `src/session-pin.ts:24-56` (bounded in-memory Map, sliding TTL, stale-entry backstop, metadata-only, no persistence — restart correctly starts at zero, exactly freellmapi's stated reasoning at ratelimit.ts:56-58). Key it on `provider` and on `provider/model`. Acquire immediately before dispatch, release in the walk's `finally`. Apply it in `orderByUsability` as a FOURTH ordering band (live → leased-at-cap → credential-faulted → cooling), never as an exclusion — that keeps "health DEMOTES, never drops", which is still in force, and it is strictly better than freellmapi's `continue` skip at router.ts:1170. Cap default: OFF (null), opt-in per provider via config, following freellmapi's own explicit judgement at ratelimit.ts:88-96 ("there is deliberately no built-in per-platform table … a wrong default is worse than none"). PRIOR ART: freellmapi server/src/services/ratelimit.ts:60-148 (Lease interface, LEASE_MAX_AGE_MS backstop at :75, `pruneLeases` :77-82, idempotent `releaseLease` :141-143, `resetLeases` test seam :146-148) and call sites server/src/services/router.ts:1170,1193,1207 (lease taken only after every gate has cleared, so a rejected candidate never consumes budget — copy that ordering). Do NOT adopt the provisional-token half (ratelimit.ts:162-193, 292-336) yet: it presupposes per-(platform,model,key) rpm/rpd/tpm/tpd limits llm-relay does not have. The `LEASE_MAX_AGE_MS`-style default is exactly the case the directive's recalibration clears — llm-relay already ships fork-validated tunable defaults (DEFAULT_WALK_BUDGET_MS at src/server.ts:1086, DEFAULT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS at :1105).

items.item: Thompson-sampled reliability (Beta posterior draw per routing decision)
items.oldReason: "llm-relay's deterministic equivalents already exist (`deploymentFitness` convex composite with provenance; neutral-50 mid-band for the unmeasured; config order as policy), and a random draw cannot answer 'why this backend' reproducibly. The un-blended `/candidates` invariant forbids a second composite score." (docs/freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:365-369)
items.rationale: The "second composite score" clause is VOIDED — and it was never sound anyway: llm-relay ALREADY runs a composite (`deploymentFitness`, 0.75·capability + 0.2·operational + 0.05·metadata, src/benchmarks.ts:221), and test/offload.test.ts:537-545 explicitly permits `sortInputs.fitness` while forbidding only a top-level `score`/`rank`/`recommendation`. The real content of that pin is decomposability, not "no composites". What SURVIVES independently is the reproducibility objection, and it rests on a goal the directive left standing, not on the struck invariant: "Transparent — the user should never have to wonder what is happening" (docs/project-goals.md:16), operationalised as provenance headers (`x-llm-relay-pool-attempts`, `x-llm-relay-degraded`, `x-llm-relay-sticky`) whose whole contract is that the served route is reconstructible from recorded state. A per-call `sampleBeta` draw (freellmapi server/src/services/scoring.ts:249-254, drawn at router.ts:826 and :1073) makes ordering irreproducible from the recorded state by construction. That is an independent technical basis, not a manufactured replacement. Residue worth naming rather than adopting: the DETERMINISTIC half of the same idea — `expectedReliability` = α/(α+β) with an explicit Beta(1,1) prior (scoring.ts:70-89) — is not random, is a well-founded "unknown is genuinely uncertain, not assumed good" rule, and is a strictly better-behaved encoding of what llm-relay does by hand with `evidenceConfidence`/`confidenceAdjustedScore` (src/benchmarks.ts:79-92). If the operational axis ever needs a success/failure prior, take that formula; do not take the sampler.

items.item: The 10% exploration floor (EXPLORE_CHANCE for unmeasured models)
items.oldReason: Bundled into "Randomness in routing" with Thompson sampling: deterministic equivalents exist, a random draw cannot answer "why this backend", and the un-blended /candidates invariant forbids a second composite score. (docs/freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:365-369)
items.rationale: The invariant clause is voided, but this item has a specific independent basis that the removal does not touch: the starvation problem an exploration floor exists to solve does not exist in llm-relay. freellmapi's own docstring states the purpose exactly — "this guarantees a floor so models with no reliability/speed data still get sampled instead of being starved by prior-heavy rivals" (server/src/services/router.ts:333-340) — i.e. it is needed because that relay learns operational quality ONLY from served traffic. llm-relay does not: `PingLoop` synthetically probes every pool member, pool heads first and then all members (src/ping/cadence.ts:59-69), results persist across restarts via probe-cache.json, and `getModelSummary`/`getMeasuredStability` feed the operational axis of `deploymentFitness` regardless of whether a member ever served a request. A never-selected member is therefore measured, not starved. Secondly, the two mechanisms have different costs: a probe spends one token at max_tokens=1, whereas an exploration floor spends 1 request in 10 of the user's REAL traffic on a model believed worse — a quality cost paid by the person the tool exists for, which fails rubric item 1 ("this installation first") independently of any struck invariant. I am not manufacturing this reason: it is the same reason recorded in the original review ('deterministic equivalents already exist'), narrowed to the one form where it is actually verifiable.

items.item: Strategy weight vectors (balanced / smartest / fastest / reliable presets + a user 'custom' vector)
items.oldReason: "The un-blended `/candidates` invariant forbids a second composite score"; grouped under "Randomness in routing" with the note that llm-relay's deterministic equivalent (`deploymentFitness` convex composite with provenance) already exists. (docs/freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:365-369)
items.rationale: This rejection rested entirely on the struck invariant, and it was self-refuting on its own terms: the argument was "we already have a convex composite", and the proposal is precisely to make that composite's weights nameable. Today those weights are hardcoded literals with no lever at all — `0.75·capability + 0.2·operational + 0.05·metadata` (src/benchmarks.ts:221) and `0.45·toolFit + 0.35·taskFit + 0.15·contextFit + 0.05·outputFit` (:219). There is no way for the owner to say "today I care about latency over capability". Partial existing substitute, stated honestly: effort pools (`pool/low|medium|high|xhigh`) give a per-request capability lever and are more transparent than a global mode — but they change pool MEMBERSHIP by capability floor, not ORDER within it, and CLAUDE.md already records that effort pools now have near-identical membership and differ only in order, so the two are converging on the same axis. CONCRETE SHAPE: `routing.fitnessWeights?: { capability, operational, metadata }` in config.json, validated and renormalized at config load (config.ts already validates whole documents; config-edit.ts already runs candidates through `loadConfig()`), defaulting to today's 0.75/0.20/0.05 so behaviour is unchanged when absent. Thread it into `deploymentFitness(strength, signals, weights)` and surface the APPLIED vector in `/candidates.sortInputs` beside the components that already travel there, so the decomposability that test/offload.test.ts:537-545 actually pins is preserved. PRIOR ART: freellmapi server/src/services/scoring.ts:36-46 (BANDIT_PRESETS as pure weight vectors — "each is just a weight vector — the engine is identical") and :270-277 (`combineScore` renormalizes a non-normalized vector so the base cannot escape [0,1] — copy that defensive renormalization). Do NOT adopt the persona names, the persisted-settings table, or the dashboard toggle; a config field with a restart is the right weight for a loopback personal tool.

items.oldReason: Same bucket as the weight vectors: deterministic equivalents exist and "the un-blended `/candidates` invariant forbids a second composite score"; hardcoded/operator-set routing tables also flagged under provider-agnosticism. (docs/freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:365-369, docs/rejection-ledger-2026-08-16.md:77-84)
items.rationale: The stated reason was the struck invariant only. The gap it fills is real and currently unfilled in llm-relay: the operator's levers on a pool member are binary — leave it in, or tombstone it out (the 2.4 pool exclude list, adopted 2026-08-14). Everything in between is evidence-derived and expiring (target-facts.ts demotions). There is no "keep it, just try it last" preference, which is exactly freellmapi's #738 motivation: "a slow, poor-quality, or just less-preferred model should be demoted without being disabled outright" (server/src/services/model-weight-overrides.ts:8-33). The surviving RECALIBRATED rule governs the shape, not the existence: an operator multiplier is a preference, not a measurement, so it must be labelled as one and must not be folded into the measured number. freellmapi already gets this right structurally by applying it AFTER `combineScore` (model-weight-overrides.ts:76-83), leaving the measured score intact. CONCRETE SHAPE: `routing.preferences?: { "<provider>/<model>": number }` in config.json (NOT an env-var JSON blob — llm-relay validates whole config documents, and an env blob is unvalidatable and invisible to `llm-relay config`), bounded to [0,2], applied after `deploymentFitness` and surfaced as its OWN `sortInputs` fields (`operatorPreference` + `fitnessAfterPreference`) beside the untouched `fitness`, so a reader can always see both the evidence and the owner's thumb on the scale. Key it provider-qualified, unlike freellmapi's deliberate model_id-only match (:28-29) — llm-relay's whole limits/price/facts model is per-(provider, model) and an unqualified key would contradict it. ALSO ADOPT the drift warning (model-weight-overrides.ts:119-185): a typo'd id silently doing nothing is the real failure mode, and llm-relay's config load already has the warn-don't-abort channel (`Config.warnings`) this belongs in.

items.item: Per-platform sampling-param droplists (PLATFORM_PARAM_POLICIES: drop / rename / jsonObjectToSchema / defaultMaxTokens)
items.oldReason: "per-platform sampling-param droplists and max_tokens floors (hardcoded provider tables)" — rejected under provider-agnosticism, i.e. no hardcoded provider knowledge in `src/`. (docs/freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:399-400, ledger C6)
items.rationale: VOIDED twice over. First by the directive. Second because the invariant was already false as applied: llm-relay ships a per-platform sampling-param droplist in `src/` today — `shouldUseDisabledThinkingForProvider` hardcodes `["cerebras","mistral","groq","sambanova"]` as providers that reject `thinking:{type:"disabled"}` (src/ping/ping.ts:59), plus a LEARNED droplist (`markDisabledThinkingUnsupported` :54, consulted :95, learned from an actual rejection :153-157). Provider knowledge also lives in src/presets.ts (bases, models, signup URLs), src/authEnv.ts:17 (per-provider env alias table) and src/refusal-interpretation.ts:417-540 (provider-specific refusal wording). The written invariant is "no hardcoded provider URLs, models, or keys in `src/`" — about routing configuration — and the C6 rejection over-read it into "no provider knowledge at all". PARTIAL INDEPENDENT RESIDUE, stated honestly: a provider that 400s on an unsupported param is already absorbed — `classifyStatus` treats 400 as retriable (src/server.ts:1069) and the pool fails over. But freellmapi's own recorded reasoning names the failure that survives: "without a ceiling the same invalid value rides every fallback candidate — the chain cannot rescue the request" (lib/sampling-params.ts:340-344). In a 15-member pool one bad param burns the entire walk, and the metadata-only log records only `errorKinds`, so it is invisible. That is a real unmitigated failure mode here, though no sighting is recorded on this install. CONCRETE SHAPE, minimal first step: lift the existing thinking-disabled droplist + its learn-on-rejection mechanism out of `src/ping/ping.ts` into a shared `src/param-policy.ts` so the DATA path can consult what the probe path already knows — today that knowledge is stranded in the prober. Then extend `refusal-interpretation.ts` with a `param-unsupported` fact kind (provider-scoped, signature = the 400 body naming the parameter) so new drops are LEARNED and reviewer-accepted rather than typed, keeping the lookup-never-inference rule intact. Only import freellmapi's static table (lib/sampling-params.ts:226-272) for entries llm-relay has itself observed — heed their own guard at :196-198: "only documented/observed rejections are listed, because wrongly dropping a working param is as bad as a 400." Skip `defaultMaxTokens`/`unifiedMaxTokensCap` entirely: llm-relay's clients always send max_tokens.

items.rationale: The invariant-based half is voided and the SQLite half is only a shape objection (llm-relay's versioned-JSON stores — target-facts.json, context-limits.json — are the equivalent substrate). But a reason the ledger never recorded survives on inspection of the source, and it is decisive: in freellmapi the quirk registry is NOT on the routing path at all. `resolveQuirksByModel` and `listQuirkDefinitions` (server/src/services/quirks.ts:24,59) have exactly one non-test consumer — `scripts/export-catalog.ts:85-86` — and the seeded content is human prose for a dashboard ("Key is account_id:token", "NIM gemma route hangs", "Daily :free cap is account-wide"; migrations/20260101_000000_legacy_baseline.ts:2104-2190). items.item: Reasoning-effort mapping tables (EFFORT_ALIASES + per-platform effort clamping)
items.oldReason: "per-model quirk and reasoning-effort tables" rejected under "Hardcoded provider tables also violate provider-agnosticism" (docs/rejection-ledger-2026-08-16.md:77-84), carried from review §5's hardcoded-provider-tables grouping.
items.rationale: The stated reason is VOIDED, but the item does not survive its own re-examination and I will not invent a replacement invariant to keep it dead — here is the actual accounting. The feature has two halves and neither stands alone in llm-relay. (i) Wire translation of `reasoning_effort` / `reasoning:{effort}` is already done by llm-bridge, which llm-relay delegates to on purpose: node_modules/llm-bridge/dist/index.js:1262, 1448-1459, 1572-1597. Re-implementing it is a genuine second implementation of a dependency's job, which is a lightweight-dependency argument, not the struck invariant. (ii) Alias coercion of non-OpenAI spellings (freellmapi lib/sampling-params.ts:42-61) has no sighting here — llm-relay's primary client speaks Anthropic Messages, where effort arrives as a `thinking` budget rather than `reasoning_effort`. (iii) The one live piece — clamping an effort to the set a platform actually accepts, so it does not 400 (sampling-params.ts:69-84, applied :302-305) — is a strict special case of the per-platform param droplist and should land there, in item 6's `param-policy` shape, not as its own table. NAMING A REAL HAZARD in adopting this standalone: llm-relay uses `low/medium/high/xhigh` as POOL names, and `xhigh` is literally one of freellmapi's effort aliases (sampling-params.ts:43). A client sending `reasoning_effort: "xhigh"` and a user asking for `pool/xhigh` are unrelated concepts, and importing an effort-alias table invites conflating a capability band with a sampling knob.

items.item: FRAMING: what "no hardcoded provider knowledge in src/" actually protected
items.oldReason: CLAUDE.md:167-169 — "No hardcoded provider URLs, models, or keys in src/. Everything comes from config... NIM/llama in src/ are doc-comment examples only."
items.rationale: The invariant as literally written is already false in llm-relay's own source, in at least seven places, three of which are on live code paths: src/presets.ts carries 9 providers' base URLs, authEnv names, tierTypes, recommendedModels AND per-provider tuning (timeoutMs 30000 sambanova / 60000 groq / 120000 nim — presets.ts:20,37,85); src/ping/quota.ts:28-30 hardcodes the literal string https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/auth/key and calls it at runtime; src/ping/ping.ts:59 is a bare ["cerebras","mistral","groq","sambanova"] behaviour table; src/refusal-interpretation.ts:417-473 is a curated seed table whose comments name HuggingFace, Ollama Cloud, NIM and Gemini by wording and which is READ ON THE REQUEST PATH; src/authEnv.ts:18-30 and src/key-import.ts:44-49 are per-provider alias lists; src/cli.ts:310-333 templates provider bases. So "NIM/llama are doc-comment examples only" is factually wrong and has been for a long time. What the rule actually protected, and what should be restated in its place: (a) adding a provider must never require a src/ change — routing resolves wholly from config (base/model/kind/authEnv/authHeader), still true and worth keeping; (b) no provider-keyed table may be UNAVOIDABLE — every one above is a default, seed or alias that config or evidence overrides, or sits off the request path; (c) no heuristic identity inference (authEnv.ts's closed alias list; target-facts.ts:74-77's refusal to infer group membership from id prefixes). (c) is a rule about heuristics, not about provider-agnosticism, and it survives on its own legs independent of C6 — it is the only part of C6 that still does load-bearing work. Relaxing C6 therefore permits a curated provider-keyed table in src/ when it is: overridable by config, inert on a miss (absence ⇒ today's behaviour), provenance-labelled where it feeds a user-visible decision, and not performing identity inference.

The third is not a reason against — it is the ARGUMENT FOR: the table exists precisely to carry the number a provider documents but does not serve in a header. And metering keys you already hold is accounting, not custody, which is exactly the distinction the owner has now reinstated as a first-class goal. Nothing independent survives. The problem is real and measured on this install: docs/pool-eligibility.md:29-30 records pool/xhigh's 15 members resolving to four independent quota domains, so failover spent 13 round-trips to learn 4 facts, and NIM (this install's primary backend) meters ~40 req/min across the whole account so every model's own rpm reads as unspent. Concrete shape: (1) add `accountLimits?: { rpm?: number; rpd?: number; tpd?: number }` to ProviderConfig (src/config.ts:59-98) beside `timeoutMs`/`stallTimeoutMs` — operator-authored, so the config half raises no invariant question at all, and `stallTimeoutMs` (config.ts:93) is the precedent for adopting a freellmapi knob this exact way. Prior art: freellmapi DEFAULT_PROVIDER_DAILY_REQUEST_CAPS (openrouter 1000, modelscope 1800) and DEFAULT_PROVIDER_MINUTE_REQUEST_CAPS (nvidia 40), both env-overridable via PROVIDER_*_CAP_<PLATFORM>. (3) The counter needs no new store: src/ping/runtime-telemetry.ts:9-24 already keeps per-(providerKey, modelId) RecentCall{timestamp, tokens} with WriteBehindTimer durability, so a provider-level rollup is an aggregation. ⚠ TWO ADAPTATIONS ARE MANDATORY, both from invariants still in force. First, enforcement must DEMOTE, never skip: freellmapi's router does `continue` past a capped key (router.ts:1164-1167), which is structurally the `filter(isHealthy)` shape that "health demotes, never drops" was written against — implement as a fourth bucket in orderByUsability (src/server.ts:1018-1043), ordered after `live`, so a pool with nothing else left still tries it. Second, our count is an estimate of OUR OWN spend, not the provider's ledger, and must be labelled as such — copy freellmapi's SOURCE_PRIORITY ranking (header/quota_api 5 > error_body 4 > probe 3 > local_usage 2 > documentation 1) so a header-observed `remaining` always outranks a locally-counted one. That ranking is the correct discharge of the recalibrated "a guess must never look like a measurement" rule, not a violation of it: the constant is tunable, the provenance is stated.

But the honest finding is that llm-relay already owns the MECHANISM and lacks only the PRIOR — and that changes the shape of the adoption, not whether to adopt. src/target-facts.ts:80-85 defines FactScope as deployment → group → provider → model resolved most-specific-first, and src/server.ts:1027-1036 already demotes every sibling behind a credential on one member's stated allowance exhaustion. Of the 25 platform lines there, ~23 encode "every model behind this credential shares one pool", which llm-relay already treats as the default. The one case llm-relay genuinely cannot express today is the SUB-PROVIDER pool: OpenRouter's :free daily cap is account-wide across all :free models but separate from the paid account pool (freellmapi keys these openrouter::free vs openrouter::account; the quirk seed or-free-cap-account-wide states it). llm-relay's FactScope {kind:"group"; members: string[]} can represent it — but nothing populates a member list. Also worth taking from the same file for near-zero cost: HEADER_SPECS, the per-platform rate-limit header names for groq/cerebras/openrouter — llm-relay reads x-ratelimit-* generically in src/ping/ping.ts but does not persist limit/remaining/reset as an observation, and those are HEADER-sourced (priority 5), i.e. the strongest accounting input available and the one that makes item C6-1's local counter checkable against reality.

items.oldReason: freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:399 — listed with sampling droplists under a single parenthetical reason, "(hardcoded provider tables)". No other reason given.
items.rationale: The one stated reason is wholly C6 and is void. Checked for an independent basis and found a partial one pointing the other way, so I record it honestly rather than manufacture a replacement: llm-relay already prefers the general form of this class of fix — src/backend.ts:507-512 drops one offending param and retries once on 400/422, and status-vs-freellmapi-2026-08-16.md:170 argues that pattern generalises with no provider table. But a max_tokens FLOOR is structurally outside that pattern: nothing 400s, the provider silently applies a tiny server-side default and the answer is truncated mid-sentence, so there is no refusal to learn from. Learn-from-the-refusal cannot cover it; only a stated default can. That is a genuine gap in llm-relay's approach, not a reason to keep the rejection. What tempers the verdict is scope, and only in its defensible form: the trigger is a client that OMITS max_tokens, and Claude Code — this relay's primary client — always sends it, so no configured provider is exposed today (and presets.ts has no Cloudflare entry, the one platform freellmapi seeds). That is a fact about the wire, not a "no user needs it" hand-wave. Concrete shape: `defaultMaxTokens?: number` on ProviderConfig (src/config.ts:84-93, beside timeoutMs/stallTimeoutMs), applied ONLY when the inbound request omits max_tokens. Do not port PLATFORM_PARAM_POLICIES to carry it. Note for the recalibrated invariant: freellmapi's 8192 is not an unprovenanced guess — sampling-params.ts:252-258 derives it as "generous for a chat turn plus reasoning, and small enough to fit inside the smallest context window in the Workers AI catalog (24K)". Under the recalibration that is a tunable constant with a stated derivation, which is permitted; what would still be forbidden is reporting it back as an observed provider limit through resolveMetadata.

items.oldReason: freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:399 — "(hardcoded provider tables)"; restated at status-vs-freellmapi-2026-08-16.md:169-170 as "never freellmapi's platform-keyed table".
items.rationale: The stated reason is C6 and is void, so the rejection survives only if something independent holds — and here something does, though it is NOT the reason that was given. The extended sampling set the table governs does not exist anywhere on llm-relay's wire: grep for top_k / min_p / logit_bias / logprobs across src/ returns zero hits, the inbound surface is Anthropic Messages translated by llm-bridge, and Claude Code sends none of them. A droplist with nothing to drop is dead code, and dead provider tables are exactly what makes future maintainers infer a policy that isn't there. ⚠ That is a fact about the code path, not the struck "no client of this relay needs it" reasoning — it would reopen the moment llm-relay grows a front that forwards these params. But the audit turned up one genuinely in-scope carve-out that should be adopted under the accounting goal, and it is worth more than the table: the ONE extra param llm-relay injects itself is `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` (src/backend.ts:492-495), whose own comment says "anything metering off the stream undercounts" without it — and src/backend.ts:507-512 drops it on a 400/422 and retries, so a backend that rejects it silently costs llm-relay its streamed token counts on EVERY request thereafter, while paying the failed round-trip each time. Two small fixes: remember per-provider that stream_options was rejected (a learned fact in the existing target-facts store, not a platform table) so the doomed first attempt is paid once; and record that provider's streamed usage as UNMEASURED rather than letting it land as 0. The second is the recalibrated invariant doing real work — a zero token count presented beside real ones is a guess wearing a measurement's clothes, and the reinstated metering goal is exactly what makes it matter.

BUT an independent technical counter survives and is strong: llm-relay already ships the deterministic, no-body-rewrite answer to the same problem — `{contextWindow}` resolves the pool's real minimum (131k-163k measured) and hands it to the child as `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS`, so the CLIENT compacts itself with full knowledge of its own history. A relay-side compressor would rewrite conversation content the client is already managing. Adopt therefore only the residue with measured pain: the 413s from oversized/base64 image blocks, which the review itself conceded are real on this install (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:333-337). Shape: a deterministic, ANNOUNCED request-size guardrail beside `estimateRequestTokens` — refuse-with-reason naming the oversized block, or drop the oldest image with an `x-llm-relay-degraded`-style header. Not the 8-engine pipeline (~1,700 lines) and not the fidelity gate.

items.oldReason: "Agentic histories never repeat byte-identical; replaying tool calls is a safety hazard" (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:393-394)
items.rationale: This reason never rested on a removed invariant — it is a factual claim about the traffic, and it holds. Every turn of an agentic conversation appends to the history, so a SHA-256 over the canonicalised request (freellmapi's key) misses by construction; the only repeating requests on this install are liveness probes (`pools --probe`, key-checker), where a cache hit would destroy the probe's entire purpose. Replaying a cached `tool_use` block is additionally a safety hazard the destructive-refusal invariant (still in force) exists to bound. One thing IS worth harvesting and it is not the cache: freellmapi states in its own header comment that the cache exists for "savings accounting" — the accounting of avoided/actual spend is now a first-class goal here, but it is served by the metering work below, with no cache required.

items.oldReason: "No client of this relay sends `response_format`; revisit if one appears" (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:397-399)
items.rationale: Pure scope reasoning, struck — and it was already wrong on its own terms, because llm-relay has an INTERNAL consumer nobody counted. The reshaper contract requires the repair model to return `{"inputs":{...}}`, and `extractJson()` (src/reshaper.ts:253-270) is precisely a JSON healer: it tries the fenced block, then the raw text, then a first-`{`/last-`}` slice. freellmapi's version is the same idea one bug further along — it also tries a `[`…`]` slice and sorts candidates LONGEST-FIRST, with a comment recording the real defect that motivated it: `According to [1], here is the JSON: {"city":"Paris"}` parsed the citation marker `[1]` as the answer, "a valid parse of the wrong value, silently delivered". llm-relay's brace-only slice is immune to that exact input but has no array-payload path at all, so a reshaper that answers with a top-level array is a total miss today. Adopt (a) NOW, cheap and high-value: add the bracket candidate and longest-first ordering to `extractJson`, with a test on freellmapi's citation-marker string. Then (b) optionally: `response_format` enforcement on the OpenAI front, non-streaming only, as a RETRIABLE dead turn that fails over WITHOUT penalising the provider's health (the model ignored the format; the provider is fine) — that failover-not-cooldown distinction is the load-bearing part.

items.rationale: Struck as stated. items.rationale: The reason had three clauses and they fare differently. "No dashboard" is struck (and see the dashboard row — a read surface for metering is now warranted). items.oldReason: "The URLs are operator-typed, not attacker-supplied" (rejection-ledger:109; status-vs-freellmapi:190-192)
items.rationale: The threat-model claim is independent of every removed invariant and it holds: freellmapi's 252-line DNS/address-class guard exists because an authenticated DASHBOARD user sets `base_url` there (its own header says so), whereas llm-relay's provider bases come from a JSON file only the operator's CLI writes — there is no HTTP path that sets a base URL. BUT while verifying I found the real adjacent gap the SSRF framing was hiding, and it is live: `fetchBackend` calls `fetchFn(target.base + args.path, init)` (src/backend.ts:428) and the direct-Chat path calls `fetchFn(target.base + "/chat/completions", …)` (src/backend.ts:946) with NO `redirect: "manual"`, while `src/ping/ping.ts:119` sets exactly that — the 2026-08-09 audit fixed credential-carrying redirects on the ping path (fcc1452) and left the request path alone. Node's fetch strips `Authorization` on a cross-origin redirect but NOT a custom header, and llm-relay's `authHeader` is configurable (`buildTargetHeaders`, src/backend.ts:909-915, e.g. `x-api-key`). So a provider base that answers 30x can carry a provider key to another origin. Adopt: `redirect: "manual"` on both backend fetches, treat a 3xx as a clean failover-eligible error, matching the ping fix. Credential containment is squarely inside what remains in force.

items.oldReason: "The called path is the stronger signal" (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:396)
items.rationale: As a ROUTING claim the reason survives, and freellmapi agrees with it — its own classifier puts the `x-claude-code-session-id` header and the wire format above the UA and calls the UA a fallback (client-classifier.ts:37-49,68-79). Nothing about routing should change. What the reason cannot survive is the reinstated accounting goal: "which client spent this quota" is now a first-class question, and `clientForPath()` answers with only four values (claude/codex/openai/default), so the main session, a `claude -p` cliLane child and an offloaded subagent are indistinguishable in every accounting record. Adopt: a coarse client-attribution enum in the metadata log ONLY, derived path/header-first with UA as the last tiebreak, never consulted by routing. ⚠ The shape matters for an invariant still in force: log the CLASSIFIED ENUM from a closed vocabulary, never the raw `user-agent` string — "logs are metadata only, never headers" is enforced at the sink by `LOG_FIELDS`, and a verbatim UA would be a header value in the log. One new allow-listed field, one closed enum.

items.oldReason: "No evidence of runaway attempts… the `x-llm-relay-max-*` request headers fail this-installation-first — no client we run will ever set them" (suggestion-review-2026-08-04.md:49-55)
items.rationale: Split the two halves. (a) CLIENT-SET relay-private headers: the stated reason is voided as scope reasoning, but the item stays dead on an independent ground — a cap a client asserts about itself is untrusted input to a spend guard, which is backwards; the operator owns the budget, not the caller. (b) BUDGETS THEMSELVES: this is the item the owner's directive most directly reopens, because a budget is the enforcement arm of a meter and metering is reinstated as a founding goal. The old bundle of reasons does not survive contact: "one place per policy" is struck; "credentials stay user-operated" is struck and was misapplied anyway (metering a key you already hold yourself is accounting, not custody); and the third reason — "free providers publish no limits to meter against" — is only half true, since `extractQuotaPercent` already parses seven `x-ratelimit-*` header pairs off REAL traffic (src/ping/ping.ts:26-52) and `fetchProviderQuota` reads OpenRouter's balance endpoint (src/ping/quota.ts:27-40). Shape: config-declared per-credential `limits: {rpm,rpd,tpm,tpd}` on the provider entry, an in-memory sliding-window counter per (provider,model,credential), and a pre-dispatch predicate that DEMOTES a credential past its cap in `orderByUsability()` — never drops it, because health-demotes-never-drops remains in force and a cap is a softer signal than a breaker trip. On the recalibrated provenance rule, state it explicitly: an operator-typed cap is a DECLARED PARAMETER, the counters are MEASUREMENTS, and a provider-stated `x-ratelimit-limit` is a third class — keep all three in separate fields with a source label (freellmapi's observation ledger already ranks sources by confidence, provider-quota.ts:58-75), and the fact that a default has to be picked is not a provenance violation. Land 1.5 (wall-clock walk budget, adoption-review:91-97) alongside it as the attempt-side bound.

items.oldReason: "Exhaustion is already self-describing… returning the last **real** upstream error beats a synthesized envelope" (suggestion-review-2026-08-04.md:87-93)
items.rationale: Two items, two fates. `route_exhausted` ENVELOPES: reason SURVIVES untouched — the real-upstream-error-beats-a-synthesized-one maxim is independent of everything removed and is reinforced by the all-429 earliest-`Retry-After` design that shipped. Keep rejected. TRACE STORE: weakened, and the accounting goal reframes it. llm-relay already has the substrate — decision 2.6 landed a bounded statuses-only `attempts[]` through the `LOG_FIELDS` sink (src/log.ts:53-54, MAX_LOG_ATTEMPTS=64, ATTEMPT_FIELDS provider/model/status/ms) with rotation (:144-150). What it lacks is two things I verified: (1) the live config sets `"log": {"level":"metadata","file":null}` (~/.llm-relay/config.json), so every accounting record is written to the stdout of a detached, non-autostarted process and is LOST — the only persisted log file, ~/.llm-relay/relay.log, is 42 lines and last written 2026-07-31 while runtime-telemetry shows 1,897 calls on one NIM model alone; and (2) the record carries no token usage at all, so spend is unreconstructible. Adopt: default `log.file` to `~/.llm-relay/requests.jsonl`, and add backend-reported input/output tokens to the record as nullable fields keeping the existing unknown-vs-zero convention (src/anthropic.ts:66-69 — an absent usage field must stay absent, never become 0). That is the accounting substrate, at a fraction of an in-memory trace store with a lookup endpoint and a versioned record schema, which stays rejected.

items.rationale: ⚠ Read the polarity: rejecting this item means KEEPING today's 400/404 failover. The reason is purely technical, touches none of the removed invariants, and has since been extended in the same direction rather than undermined — adoption item 1.4 added 410/End-of-Life as retriable AND learnable after NVIDIA served real 410s on this machine on 2026-08-07, and `carriesEligibilityFact` reads those bodies. The live follow-up in this area is the opposite of removal: §3.3's ADAPT to SALVAGE a tool call from a 4xx `failed_generation` body before discarding the turn — which only works because 400 stays retriable.

items.oldReason: Bundled into "extra wire surfaces… no client that can reach this relay speaks them" (status-vs-freellmapi-2026-08-16.md:187-189), while §4.2 of the same doc concedes it is a real gap
items.rationale: The bundling was the error: this is not an extra wire surface, it is the surface llm-relay's entire premise rests on. Every supported client is pointed at `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, and `GET /v1/models` on that base is answered today with a Codex/OpenAI-shaped payload — `{object:"list", data, models}` where each entry carries `slug`, `supported_reasoning_levels`, `shell_type`, `base_instructions` and no `type:"model"`, no `created_at`, and the envelope has no `has_more`/`first_id`/`last_id` (src/routes/admin.ts:36-66,135-140). An Anthropic-SDK client listing models gets a non-conformant response from an Anthropic-shaped endpoint. Adopt freellmapi's exact mechanism: content-negotiate on the `anthropic-version` REQUEST header inside the existing handler — present ⇒ emit `{data:[{type:"model",id,display_name,created_at}], has_more:false, first_id, last_id}`, absent ⇒ the current Codex/OpenAI payload unchanged. No new route, no new dependency, ~20 lines, and it composes with the `/livez` work above.

items.oldReason: "No consumer in this topology" / "no dashboard, no writeback, nothing to protect" (freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:402-403; status-vs-freellmapi:187-189)
items.rationale: Voided, and the reinstated goal supplies the missing consumer directly: metering nobody can read is not accounting. It is also the item that makes several other rejections in this group circular — "no dashboard" was itself the reason given for the catalog-override rejection. What must NOT be adopted is freellmapi's actual dashboard: 76 `.tsx` files plus i18n, theming, auth and a desktop tray build — a second product, and it presupposes the DB. Shape for llm-relay: (1) primary surface is the CLI — a `llm-relay usage` view aggregating the JSONL request log plus `runtime-telemetry.json` by provider/model/client/day, which is where every other status answer here already lives (`keys`, `pools --probe`, `candidates`, `telemetry`); (2) optional second surface is ONE self-contained static HTML page served by `handleAdminRoutes()`. Two constraints from what remains in force: it must be token-gated, unlike `/telemetry`, because remaining-quota and spend are more sensitive than health; and it must be GET-only, since serving HTML from the listener widens exactly the cross-origin surface the `/offload`+`/dispatch` admission checks (src/server.ts:94-99) were built to close. Sequence it AFTER the log-persistence and token-recording fixes — a dashboard over data that is currently written to a lost stdout would render an empty page.

items.item: In-flight lease budgets (per-deployment/per-credential concurrency leases; freellmapi `services/ratelimit.ts`)
items.oldReason: "llm-relay built and then deleted this exact machinery — the unadopted kernel lease budgets removed 2026-08-04, whose rebuilding CLAUDE.md explicitly warns against." (docs/rejection-ledger-2026-08-16.md:131; docs/freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md:341-350)
items.rationale: Voided TWICE, and the second reason matters more than the directive. (1) The owner retired "built it, deleted it" as reasoning. (2) The claim is factually false: what was deleted at 27b7a48 was `RequestBudget` (27b7a48^:src/kernel/request-lifecycle.ts:84-133) — an INTRA-request attempt-count cap plus a wall-clock deadline and a cancellation signal, scoped to one request and discarded when it ends. The proposal is a CROSS-request counter of attempts currently in the air per deployment/credential, whose entire purpose is to let concurrent request A see request B. Different scope, different lifetime, opposite direction of visibility. "This exact machinery" was never built here. Stripping this reason leaves only the Group-E evidence gate (ledger:124, "until 429 storms are a measured problem") — the ledger's own §5 flags that as an unmeasured worst-case estimate that overruled the reviewer who ranked it highest — and the C4 "one place per policy" objection, which the directive removed outright. SHAPE: the begin/complete handshake this needs already exists and is the one kernel piece that survived. Increment a counter in `CircuitBreaker.beginAttempt` (src/circuit-breaker.ts:190) and decrement in `completeAttempt` (src/circuit-breaker.ts:253), keyed by the same `getKey(target)` the circuit state already uses (src/circuit-breaker.ts:165-169); both transitions are already one-shot with duplicate/cross-target/foreign-handle guards, so double-count is structurally impossible. Feed `inFlight(target)` into `orderByUsability` (src/server.ts:1018) as a TIE-BREAK WITHIN the live band only — never as a filter — which keeps "health demotes, never drops" (still in force) intact and answers the C2 objection that killed scoped breakers. A hard cap is opt-in per provider (`provider.maxConcurrent`, default null = unlimited), which is exactly freellmapi's own reasoning: ratelimit.ts:84-96 refuses a built-in per-platform table because "a wrong default is worse than none." That also satisfies the RECALIBRATED C5 — a null-defaulted operator-set cap is a tunable constant, not a guess wearing a measurement's label; nothing is presented as observed. Add the stale-lease backstop (freellmapi ratelimit.ts:71-82, `LEASE_MAX_AGE_MS`); it is needed here specifically because only the Anthropic path force-completes an outstanding attempt (src/server.ts:872-882) — see the separate finding. Carry `estimateRequestTokens()` on the lease as a token weight (freellmapi ratelimit.ts:60-66, 171-178): that is the join between this and the reinstated metering goal, since provisional token accounting is what closes the check-then-act race the reactive breaker cannot see. Do NOT adopt freellmapi's DB-backed RPM/RPD/TPM/TPD gates in the same change — those are a separate ledger item with a separate reason.

items.item: Coordinated routing refactor / central route executor (the refactor framing)
items.oldReason: "Retroactively justifies the ~85% of `src/kernel/` that nothing used; resolves the half-built kernel in the wrong direction. Policy is already shared via `classifyStatus()`/`shouldTryNext()` with pinning tests." (docs/rejection-ledger-2026-08-16.md:132; docs/suggestion-review-2026-08-04.md:30-40)
items.rationale: Two legs, and they must be scored separately rather than as one reason. LEG A — "retroactively justifies the deleted kernel / resolves the half-built kernel in the wrong direction" — is VOIDED: it is the retired reasoning, and it is now moot in both directions since the surface it referred to no longer exists to be justified. LEG B — "the policy is already shared; replacing working loops with a typed-decision executor is structure-first churn with no behavior change" (suggestion-review-2026-08-04.md:36-40) — is INDEPENDENT of the retired invariant and SURVIVES, verified: `classifyStatus` and `shouldTryNext` (src/server.ts:1066, 1074) are genuinely the single policy and both loops call them (712/718 and 1834/1839), along with `orderByUsability`, the pool-429 accumulator, `observeContextLimit` and `observeAttemptHeaders`. Leg B is also STRONGER now than when written: `test/cross-front-convergence.test.ts` landed 2026-08-14 and drives a twelve-row failure matrix (401, 429, Retry-After, 402, 5xx, transport reset, timeout, all-429 exhaustion, degraded tail, freeOnly ×2) through all three fronts with ≥2 candidates per row. That is a direct behavioral guarantee of exactly what the executor was proposed to guarantee structurally, at a fraction of the risk to the riskiest code in the repo. I am not manufacturing this reason to keep the rejection alive — it is quoted from the original review and I verified it against source. Honest counterweight, recorded rather than suppressed: the repo has now shipped FOUR instances of cross-front drift (pool-failover accounting; the context guardrail gated to /v1/messages until 0.17.0; dialect rescue uncovered on the OpenAI direct front until 0.36.x; and the attempt-completion backstop below), so the drift risk is real and recurring. But each was closed by extending a shared helper and adding a convergence row, never by unifying the loops — and that response is now systematic. REJECT the coordinated refactor and the executor rewrite; adopt the narrow residue as its own finding. Stated explicitly because the directive reinstates it: this rejection does not stand in metering's way — per-key accounting hooks onto the existing begin/complete lifecycle, not onto a route executor.

items.item: Typed failure decisions (the second half of the F2 ledger row)
items.oldReason: Bundled into the same row as the coordinated refactor and rejected with it (docs/rejection-ledger-2026-08-16.md:132)
items.rationale: Separated out because the ledger row bundles it with the refactor and it deserves its own answer. Its rejection never rested on "built it, deleted it" at all — it rests on the capability already existing, which is a Group-A style reason and is verifiable: `classifyStatus` returns a four-value typed enum (`ok`/`retriable`/`credential`/`client`) with a documented per-status rationale (src/server.ts:1066-1076), and `AttemptOutcome` (src/kernel/contracts.ts:44-75) is already a discriminated failure union carrying `failure` kind, `provenance`, `status` and `retryAfterMs`. The typed half of the proposal is substantially already implemented and survived the 2026-08-04 deletion precisely because it was load-bearing. Nothing here reopens.

items.item: Attempt-completion backstop is Anthropic-path-only (the narrow structural residue the executor would have swept up)
items.oldReason: Not separately adjudicated — it was inside the coordinated-refactor bundle
items.rationale: Surfaced while checking whether Leg B of the F2 rejection is still true. The Anthropic loop's `finally` force-completes any outstanding attempt — cancelled if the client hung up, else a `mapping`/`relay-mapper-defect` 502 (src/server.ts:872-882). The OpenAI front's `finally` (src/server.ts:1998-2001) only clears the timer and detaches the close listener; there is no `if (attempt && !attempt.completed)` backstop. So an escape path on that front leaves a begun attempt permanently uncompleted. Today the cost is bounded (a missing health data point), which is why it has gone unnoticed — but it becomes load-bearing the moment an in-flight counter rides on the same handshake, because an uncompleted attempt is a permanently leaked lease. Fix: hoist the completion backstop into a shared helper called from both fronts' `finally`, and add a client-disconnect row to `test/cross-front-convergence.test.ts` (the matrix currently has no cancellation/abort case). This is the same shape as the four prior drift incidents and is cheap; it is also the prerequisite that makes the lease safe, alongside — not instead of — the stale backstop.

items.item: Token metering is wired to the response but discarded before it is recorded
items.oldReason: Not a ledger rejection — surfaced by re-adjudicating against the reinstated accounting-and-metering goal
items.rationale: Raised because the directive reinstates per-key accounting and metering as a first-class goal, and this is the concrete state of it. The store already has the field: `ModelTelemetry.totalCompletionTokens` (src/ping/runtime-telemetry.ts:22) and the optional `RecentCall.tokens` (:13), summed at :110/:117. Real provider-reported usage is already on the path in both directions — `backend.ts:675-684` maps `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens` into Anthropic `usage`, `backend.ts:758-828` maps it back, and `backend.ts:495` sets `stream_options.include_usage` so streamed responses report it too. But the sole call site, `recordCall` (src/server.ts:1258-1263), passes only `{ ok, latencyMs }` and never `completionTokens`. `totalCompletionTokens` is therefore structurally always 0 for every deployment: the accounting field exists, the measurement exists, and the wire between them was never run. This is one call-site change to start metering real tokens rather than an estimate, and it needs no new store, no DB, and no invariant relaxation — worth confirming as the first concrete step on the reinstated goal before any windowed ledger is designed on top. Note it is also the number an in-flight lease's token weight should prefer once available (freellmapi uses an estimate at selection time by necessity, ratelimit.ts:126-137, because the real figure only arrives after the call).

items.item: Adaptive per-target timeouts (500 tok/s in, 8 tok/s out, 1.5×p95, 15s floor)
items.oldReason: "The formula is made of guesses … baked into the request path — numbers with no provenance, in a repo whose core rule is that a guess must never look like a measurement." Plus: "There is no observed timeout pain; the flat per-provider timeoutMs is comprehensible and sufficient" and "variable per-attempt deadlines also make behavior harder to reason about — anti-transparency."
items.rationale: The provenance half is VOIDED, and demonstrably so — the repo itself stopped applying it nine days later. src/server.ts:1086 ships DEFAULT_WALK_BUDGET_MS = 45_000 and src/server.ts:1105 ships DEFAULT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000, both on the request path, both justified in-comment only as "fork-validated in freellmapi" — i.e. exactly "a number with no provenance", landed 2026-08-13 (c714774) and 2026-08-14 (ed2499f) against a rejection dated 2026-08-04. The same is true of far more consequential constants that predate both: src/ping/metrics.ts:81-86 builds the stability score that ORDERS candidates out of 5000/2000/3000 ms divisors and 0.3/0.3/0.2/0.2 weights; src/benchmarks.ts:219-221 blends 0.75/0.20/0.05 and 0.45/0.35/0.15/0.05; src/benchmarks.ts:149-154 sets effort floors at 50/60/70/80; src/benchmarks.ts:211-212 log-scales against 8_192–1_048_576. None of these is labelled a measurement and none was ever challenged. The invariant was being applied to one proposal, not to the codebase. TWO independent reasons survive, and they change the shape rather than the verdict. (a) The pain is now largely fixed by a better mechanism: adoption §1.2's stall watchdog (src/server.ts:788-792) disarms the total deadline at stream commit and re-arms on every byte, which is precisely the failure mode adaptive timeouts targeted (healthy long generation killed at a flat deadline). (b) The p95-derived half is unfounded on its own terms, independent of any invariant: llm-relay's p95 comes from probes sending `"hi"` with max_tokens:1 (src/ping/ping.ts:92-93), so it measures the network round-trip, not generation time; scaling a generation deadline off it is a category error, and the 500/8 tok-per-second figures are fabricated per-model throughput presented as if they described the deployment — that specific part is still what the recalibrated rule forbids. ADOPT the residue, not the formula: (1) split a `firstByteTimeoutMs` axis off the total so the pre-commit window is tunable separately from generation — freellmapi separates exactly this (server/src/lib/provider-timeout.ts:14-19; SseStreamOptions at server/src/providers/base.ts:197-207, with `timeoutBounds: 'headers' | 'request'` at :185-194); (2) close the buffered gap — src/server.ts:624 arms one flat timer that is cleared only on the streaming path, so a slow non-streamed completion still dies at 120s with no failure evidence; (3) if any derived deadline lands, report it (`x-llm-relay-deadline: 42000 (…)` and a log field) so it is labelled rather than hidden, which is what actually answers the anti-transparency objection. Reinstated-accounting angle: none directly, but a per-attempt deadline that is reported becomes an accountable field rather than invisible behaviour.
