items.oldReason: "Never 'fix' an unknown with a large speculative value. Measured pool minimums here are 131,072–163,840 — below the 200k the claude CLI already assumes — so a speculative 1M would overshoot the weakest member eightfold. Same reasoning as 'the context guardrail fires only on a limit the serving provider published': a number nobody published is worse than no number."
items.rationale: The reason SURVIVES as stated, and it is not actually a labelling argument — it is a consequence argument backed by a measurement taken on this machine: an invented ceiling ABOVE the real one makes the client send tokens the backend rejects (src/dispatch.ts:294-298). Removing the labelling invariant does not touch that; a speculative 1M ceiling labelled `assumed` still overflows the backend. So REJECT the proposal as framed. But the rejection over-reached in one narrow, checkable way, and the recalibration is what exposes it: refusing to state a number does not produce silence. When nothing resolves, src/dispatch.ts:419 and :437 DROP the token from args and env, and the repo's own premise (src/dispatch.ts:285-287) is that the `claude` CLI then assumes 200k — above every measured pool minimum (131k–163k). The status quo therefore delegates the guess to a client that guesses HIGHER, i.e. it produces the exact overflow the rule exists to prevent, just with the relay's fingerprints off it. The safe direction is downward, and the machinery to say so already exists. ADAPT, narrowly: when a spec or pool resolves zero members, emit a conservative floor at or below the measured minimum, carried as a fourth `ContextWindowSource` value (`"assumed"`) alongside the existing `observed|provider|snapshot` (src/metadata.ts:174), surfaced on `DispatchLane.contextWindowSource` (src/dispatch.ts:108-115) beside the existing `contextWindowUnknownMembers`. Understating costs early compaction (capacity, recoverable); overstating costs a rejected request. Do NOT extend this to members that DO resolve — the existing minimum-across-resolving rule (src/dispatch.ts:300-301) is correct and better evidenced. Note this stays clear of the still-in-force health-demotes-never-drops rule: it adds a number, it never removes a candidate.

items.item: The neutral-50 mid-band (and the rejection of freellmapi's median-rank seeding as "already implemented")
items.oldReason: "Median rank seeding — 'unknown is not worst' already implemented as neutral-50 with basis labelling."
items.rationale: Nothing to reopen, and this is the item that shows where the invariant is doing REAL work — it should be the reference implementation the recalibrated rule is calibrated against, not a candidate for removal. Note first that 50 IS a tunable constant with no external provenance, shipped on the request path, and it has never been controversial. What makes it acceptable is exactly the essence the owner retained: it is labelled and confined. `Strength` carries `basis: "snapshot" | "neutral"` (src/benchmarks.ts:6, :145) so a neutral 50 is never mistaken for a 50 measured across five leaderboards; `BASIS_CONFIDENCE` is documented as "How much a basis is worth as a TIE-BREAK only. Never mixed into the score itself" (src/benchmarks.ts:231-232); the breaker exposes `getMeasuredStability(): number | null` plus `hasObservations()` and the old scalar accessor is deleted with the reasoning kept in place — "a `number` return cannot say 'nothing was measured': every caller received a plausible score and none could tell a guess from an observation" (src/circuit-breaker.ts:553-559); the placeholder is applied locally in ordering only (src/circuit-breaker.ts:583-595); `/candidates` never emits the scalar without `strengthBasis` + `strengthSignals` (src/candidates.ts:409-418); and the CLI legend says out loud "A blank cell means NOT MEASURED" and marks borrowed figures with `~` (src/cli.ts:1664-1678). That is the whole distinction the owner drew: a tunable constant used for ORDERING and labelled is fine; a placeholder reported as an observation is not. It also directly serves the reinstated accounting goal — a meter can only be honest if unknown reads as blank rather than zero.

items.item: The "no hardcoded-table rung" rule in resolveMetadata (deletion of the blanket 128k/4096 table in 0.7.0)
items.oldReason: "There is deliberately no third rung. A hardcoded table used to sit here, handing out a blanket 128k/4096 for anything it did not recognise; a guess presented as a limit is worse than a null, because callers cannot tell it apart from a measurement." Carried a second reason in the adoption review — a hardcoded provider table would violate provider-agnosticism (C6) — and a third, that limits are per-(provider,model).
items.rationale: Three reasons were bundled; they come apart cleanly now. (1) The provider-agnosticism reason is VOIDED outright — "no hardcoded provider knowledge in src/" is a removed invariant, so a per-provider table is no longer forbidden as such. (2) The per-deployment reason SURVIVES untouched: the same model id on two providers is two deployments, and any table must therefore be keyed per (provider, model), never per model id. (3) The labelling reason SURVIVES in essence but is now satisfiable rather than prohibitive — and this is precisely the overextension the owner named. "A guess presented as a limit is worse than a null" is an argument against the PRESENTATION, and the whole consumer chain already threads provenance: `MetadataSource` (src/metadata.ts:11), per-field source labels through resolveMetadata (src/metadata.ts:71-93), the `~` marker and blank-means-not-measured legend in the CLI (src/cli.ts:1676-1677), `ContextWindowSource` in dispatch. Adding a third labelled rung is mechanically cheap because the labels already exist. ADAPT: reinstate a third rung as `MetadataSource = "provider" | "reference" | "assumed"`, sourced from a checked-in per-(provider,model) table where each row carries a date and a source URL — never a blanket constant, which is what the deleted table actually was and what made it indefensible (a universal 128k/4096 tells you nothing a client did not already assume). Two hard constraints: the `assumed` rung must NOT feed the guardrail's fail-closed decision (see the next finding), and it must render distinctly from `~` in every display. The value is concentrated where publication is genuinely absent — NIM publishes no limits at all (src/catalog.ts `limits()` returns null there) and is this install's primary backend, so 0 of 29 `pool/high` members carry a provider-published window. The remaining honest cost is not an invariant but a maintenance treadmill against provider drift; CLAUDE.md's "capability data is synced, never typed" argues for harvesting into `scripts/sync-tiers.mjs` where anything is publishable and hand rows only where nothing is. Accounting tie-in: the price half of resolveMetadata is what a spend meter multiplies by, so a labelled `assumed` price rung makes metering possible on unpriced free deployments — provided the meter reports the basis alongside the figure.

items.item: The refusal to fill an unknown limit (context guardrail stays silent; no fallback ceiling)
items.oldReason: "Enforced ONLY against a limit the serving provider published about its own deployment. An unknown limit means no guardrail: the request goes upstream and the provider answers with its own (authoritative) error." And: "Don't reintroduce a fallback ceiling: a 400 invented from a number we made up is worse than a true upstream error."
items.rationale: This one has a fully independent basis and should not be reopened. The argument is not about labelling at all — it is about the DIRECTION of the failure. The guardrail's action is to prune candidates and, when all are pruned, to fail closed with a synthesized 400 (src/server.ts:535-561). A fallback ceiling that is too low therefore blocks a request that would have succeeded, using a number the relay invented, and no amount of labelling on the 400 gives the caller their answer back. Two rules that remain explicitly in force independently forbid it: "health DEMOTES candidates; it never drops them" (a ceiling nobody published removing a candidate is a drop on non-evidence), and the repo-wide maxim that a true upstream error beats a synthesized one — the same maxim that governs the all-429 policy and the pool-attempts header, not the guess invariant. It also composes with a real learning loop: the upstream error the relay lets through is what src/context-limits.ts parses into a first-party ceiling for next time, so silence here is what generates the measurement. freellmapi independently arrives at the same published-only shape (server/src/services/router.ts:1333: `entry.context_window != null && estimatedTokens > entry.context_window`). ONE narrow sub-rule inside this item IS overextended and is worth a separate small adoption — see the next finding.

items.item: Sub-rule of the above: context-limits.ts discards a DERIVED upper bound ("we sent ~N and it was refused")
items.oldReason: "Only an explicitly STATED maximum is recorded. 'We sent an estimated N tokens and it was rejected' is not a limit — it is an upper bound on a number this proxy estimated at four characters per token, and persisting it would put a guess into the one store whose whole value is that it contains measurements. If nothing parses, nothing is learned. Same rule as resolveMetadata: no rung may be a guess."
items.rationale: This is the sharpest case of the invariant blocking real evidence rather than a mislabel. A refusal that llm-relay could not parse a maximum out of is still first-party evidence: it proves the deployment's ceiling lies BELOW whatever was actually sent. The stated objection is entirely about contamination of a store — "persisting it would put a guess into the one store whose whole value is that it contains measurements" — which the recalibration answers directly: contamination is a keying-and-labelling problem, and target-facts.ts already exists precisely so that scope and kind are explicit per fact rather than reinvented per store. ADAPT: record it as a DISTINCT fact kind (`context-limit-bound`) at deployment scope with basis `estimated`, never merged into the `context-limit` value that observedContextLimit() returns, and never readable by contextWindowResolver's `observed` rung. Use it for ORDERING only — demote that deployment for requests whose estimate exceeds the bound — which keeps it on the right side of health-demotes-never-drops and of the previous finding, since it can only change who is tried first, never fail a request closed. Genuine residual risk to state honestly: the bound is expressed in this proxy's own chars/4 units (src/metadata.ts:151-171), which can be off by a wide margin on non-English or code-heavy prompts, so the bound can sit below the true ceiling and demote a deployment that would have served — that is exactly why it must demote and never prune. Value is concrete: `looksLikeContextLengthError` already recognises the error class that `parseStatedContextLimit` then throws away when no pattern matches (src/context-limits.ts:42-75), so today a recognised over-length refusal from a provider whose wording is not in the five-pattern set teaches the relay nothing at all.

items.item: Estimator-as-guess blocking per-request token accounting (raised against the reinstated accounting-and-metering goal)
items.oldReason: Not a listed rejection, but the same invariant is the operative bar: backend.ts refuses to synthesize usage — "A usage object with no numeric fields is not a measurement. Keep the relay's unknown-vs-zero convention instead of manufacturing a cost report for an upstream that omitted usage" — and estimateRequestTokens is documented as an estimate that must not "masquerade as a measurement".
items.rationale: Raising this because the task asks for adjudication against the reinstated accounting-and-metering goal, and C5 is what currently stands between the relay and any meter at all. There is today NO per-request token accounting: LOG_FIELDS (src/log.ts:77-93) has no token field, ATTEMPT_FIELDS is `{provider, model, status, ms}` (src/log.ts:95), and runtime telemetry stores only `completionTokens` (src/ping/runtime-telemetry.ts:13, :117) — so the relay cannot answer "how many tokens did this key spend today", which the owner names as one of the founding design goals. The refusal to manufacture usage (src/backend.ts:814-819) is CORRECT and should stay: a fabricated `usage` object on the wire is a lie to the client. But it does not follow that the relay's own metering ledger must be empty when an upstream omits usage — which on this install's free pool is common. ADOPT: record input/output tokens per attempt in the metadata-only log and in a per-(provider, model, credential) rolling ledger, each entry carrying `usageSource: "upstream" | "estimated"`, where `estimated` is filled from the existing single estimator (src/metadata.ts:151). That is a derived number honestly labelled at the point of use — the recalibration's central allowance — and it keeps the still-in-force metadata-only logging rule intact, since token COUNTS are metadata and no content is retained. Two constraints inherited from what remains in force: the ledger must never mix an `estimated` count into a figure presented as billed, and any cost figure must stay null where price is null (src/metadata.ts:78-88) unless the `assumed` price rung from the resolveMetadata finding lands with its basis attached. Prior art for the ledger shape, not for its custody half: freellmapi keys sliding RPM/RPD/TPM/TPD windows per (platform, model, key) at server/src/services/ratelimit.ts:314-335 with provider-wide daily caps at :561-572, and feeds them an estimate — note its own default is a bare `estimatedTokens = 1000` (server/src/services/router.ts:1329), which is weaker than what llm-relay can do with its real estimator. Adopt the metering; the key-pooling and rotation halves are a separate question belonging to group C1.
